S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with an initial account of the event and any known safety implications. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a credible risk requiring a warning or action to protect people or property. Reports and notices must not be delayed while cause is investigated.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model exceeding the 5% failure-rate benchmark must undergo regulator-supervised review and corrective-action planning, taking account of test uncertainty and real-world safety evidence. Regulators may restrict sales where necessary to address an imminent or material safety risk. Regulators must not publish a company's individual per-model failure rates; they may publish aggregated or anonymized results.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible shut-off method. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that lack this capability within six years of adoption, prioritizing units presenting the greatest safety risk. If a unit cannot be safely retrofitted, the manufacturer must notify its owner and provide an alternative protective measure, subject to regulator oversight.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must provide regulators with evidence that the suppression system is effective and does not introduce other material safety risks.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 validated thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers and regulators of newly identified material risks and provide timely safety notices with any protective actions customers should take.

document.section_notes: S2 sets a 5% per-model failure benchmark that triggers review and corrective planning but never forces a sales stop, and bars public publication of individual per-model rates while requiring numeric rates to customers. S5 makes recall mandatory at 8 per 100,000 with no transition, which directly threatens Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9), while S3's six-year retrofit window and S4's 36-month suppression deadline sit at the edges of the acceptable ranges. Both companies' red lines appear to be met, but the rules favour Northwind more.
